title: GraphRAG decision
summary: Compare graph retrieval with a simpler baseline using the questions your project needs to answer.

sections.label: Documented options
sections.text: Microsoft GraphRAG offers local graph/text retrieval and global community-summary search. Global search can be resource intensive.

sections.label: Project recommendation
sections.text: Measure a simpler retrieval baseline first. If a curated RDF graph already exists, include relevant SPARQL queries in that comparison. Preserve reviewed relationships when evaluating model-extracted alternatives.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: The alternative improves needed-evidence retrieval or answer quality enough to justify indexing cost, maintenance, and version handling.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Compare feasible approaches, Plan the evidence, Recommend go or no-go. Use when comparing GraphRAG with a simpler retrieval baseline, planning representative evidence cases and deciding whether its added work is justified. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Record the baseline, actual query strategy, corpus and index revisions, and expected evidence for each question.
Check output to obtain: Compare retrieved support, answer quality, indexing effort and query cost on the same permitted cases.
Check output to obtain: Publish a decision with observed advantages, failure cases and unmeasured claims. Inclusion does not establish a performance improvement.

catalog.applicability: Use this when considering Microsoft GraphRAG or another graph retrieval approach for your project. Measure a simpler retrieval baseline first, and include relevant SPARQL queries in the comparison if a curated RDF graph already exists.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
